text:
Predicates:
ManagedBuilding(x) ::: x is a managed building.
Pet(x) ::: x is a pet.
Allowed(x, y) ::: x is allowed in y.
Deposit(x, y) ::: the security deposit for x is y.
Rent(x, y) ::: the monthly rent for x is y.
Cat(x) ::: x is a cat.
Dog(x) ::: x is a dog.
Person(x) ::: x is a person.
Owns(x, y) ::: x owns y.
Premises:
∃x (ManagedBuilding(x) ∧ ∃y (Pet(y) ∧ Allowed(y, x))) ::: Pets are allowed in some managed buildings.
∀x (ManagedBuilding(x) → ∃y (Deposit(x, y))) ::: A deposit is required to rent an apartment in a managed building.
∀x (ManagedBuilding(x) → ∀y (Deposit(x, y) → (y ≥ Rent(x) ∨ y = Rent(x)))) ::: The security deposit can be either equal to one month's rent or more.
Cat(fluffy) ∧ Owns(tom, fluffy) ::: Fluffy is Tom's cat.
∀x (Cat(x) → Pet(x)) ::: Cats are pets.
ManagedBuilding(oliveGarden) ::: The Olive Garden is a managed building.
Rent(oliveGarden, 2000) ::: The monthly rent at the Olive Garden is $2000.
(∃x (ManagedBuilding(x) ∧ Allowed(fluffy, x) ∧ Deposit(x, y) ≤ 1500) ↔ Rents(tom, x)) ::: Tom will rent an apartment in a managed building if and only if he is allowed to move in with Fluffy, and the security deposit is no more than $1500.
2000 > 1500 ::: 2000$ is more than $1500.
Conclusion:
Rents(tom, oliveGarden) ::: Tom will rent an apartment in The Olive Garden.
